 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Under the tutelage of assistant coach Alex Tanguay , the Detroit Red Wings put one of the NHL's better power plays on the ice over the past two seasons.
 This season, the Detroit power play has slipped noticeably. And for the time being, Tanguay has slipped away from the Red Wings.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Alex is away from the team right now," Red Wings coach Todd McLellan told reporters following Tuesday's practice. "We've given him some time, and he'll be back soon."
 A 3-point night by Alex Tanguay helped him get his day with the #StanleyCup ! #FranchiseClassics continues with Game 7 of the 2001 #StanleyCup Final at 4pm ET. @Avalanche pic.twitter.com/sCTzWGV0ch 
 — NHL Media (@NHLMedia) July 17, 2019 
 No reason was given for Tanguay's absence from the team.
 The Red Wings hired Tanguay on June 30, 2021. He is the only coach on the current staff who also worked under previous Detroit head coaches Jeff Blashill and Derek Lalonde .
 In Absentia, Tanguay Still Helping Red Wings
 Under Tanguay, Detroit's power play was the fourth-best in the NHL in 2024-25, clicking at an impressive 27.0% success rate. Last season, the Red Wings' power play slipped to 12th overall in the league, but was still at 22.6%.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement This season, minus Patrick Kane and, for the most part, Dylan Larkin , the Detroit power play has slid to 18th in the NHL. It shows a 20.6% proficiency.
 In Tanguay's absence, McLellan is expecting everyone on the staff to help fill the void.
 "All of us have to take more on," McLellan said. "Alex was primarily responsible for the power play and a lot of the offensive part of the game. We've spread that out amongst our staff.
 "Power play. I'm looking at it a little bit more right now."
 Even though he's not with the Red Wings in person, Tanguay remains a contributor.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Alex is still working on the power play," McLellan said. "He's sending his cut-ups and his information to us, and we're using it.
 "So it's not like he's out of sight or out of mind. He's still part of it."
 Blais Replacing Tanguay on Red Wings Bench
 Helping out on the Detroit bench during games in Tanguay's absence is skills coach Dwayne Blais .

 "His biggest role would be to communicate with the video people on any type of challenge, because we don't have a lot of time," McLellan said. "It comes instantly through his earpiece, and then he starts to work on that.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "And then [Blais is involved] a lot of the line matching and what might be coming, a few adjustments on the bench that he can work individually with the players.
 "I think it's really good, and we should probably think about doing this more, bringing different people on the bench that have an impact in the organization."
